body:
This could be a good opportunity to show a concrete example of a buffer that is 16-byte aligned and one that isn't (using a code sample). It's common for users to be confused about what 16-byte alignment actually means for graphics programming, since things that *look* 16-byte aligned (`float; float; float; vec3`) are not always actually aligned like the graphics API expects. (In contrast, `vec3; float; float; float` is 16-byte aligned.)

This could be worth exploring in more detail in the compositor documentation, but I think the class reference should have a concise example of this at least.
